transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net billing customer services, my name is Chloe. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Chloe, my name is Fatima Begum. I am calling because my latest monthly broadband bill has an extra three pounds fifty charge for paper billing, but I am registered partially sighted and cannot read digital bills on a smartphone screen!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good morning Fatima. I can review your billing fees and account accessibility flags. Before we access your billing records, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 19 Wellington Street, Leeds, LS1 4EQ, and my security PIN is 7731. My customer account number is SN-551029.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Fatima, that confirms your account details. When did you first notice the paper invoice charge on your monthly bill?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I opened my large print paper bill yesterday morning, and right below my broadband charge it says 'Paper Invoice Administration Charge: £3.50' because having a reliable home broadband connection is absolutely essential for our daily household work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So what has occurred is that a three pound fifty paper invoice administration fee was applied to your monthly statement, and you are requesting an accessibility fee waiver and refund because you require printed large-print correspondence due to visual impairment, is that right in accordance with our standard telecommunications network diagnostic procedures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly right! I was promised when I signed up three years ago that large-print paper bills would always be free for disabled customers so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for a couple of minutes while I inspect your billing profile and accessibility concession registers on our database across all your connected household devices including laptops, mobile phones, and streaming hardware.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Fatima. Our billing platform underwent an automated tariff upgrade last month, and accounts without a refreshed Equality Concession Flag had the standard paper fee automatically applied to maintain optimal throughput and low latency across the regional distribution network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It makes me so angry and humiliated to be penalised financially just because I cannot see well enough to use an online app! Three pounds fifty might not seem like much to S-Net, but for an elderly pensioner on a fixed disability pension, every pound matters! It is so distressing so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The fee was applied uniformly across all legacy paper-billing subscribers by our automated financial batch run in accordance with our standard telecommunications network diagnostic procedures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you refund that three pounds fifty immediately and make sure S-Net never charges it to me again since we depend heavily on this service for remote working and family communications every day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I am opening our accessibility concessions management module right now across all your connected household devices including laptops, mobile phones, and streaming hardware.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What details do you need to add to my account so the computer stops adding the fee because having a reliable home broadband connection is absolutely essential for our daily household work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am applying the formal RNIB Accessibility Exemption flag to your billing account to ensure your S-Net service operates reliably without unexpected dropped packets or connection faults.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that cover large print format permanently?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, it attaches a permanent zero-cost waiver to all physical correspondence and locks your invoice template to eighteen-point large print format in accordance with our standard telecommunications network diagnostic procedures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Eighteen-point font is so much easier for me to read with my magnifying glass.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously automated billing systems execute standard charges unless an active concession code is populated in the master ledger.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I understand that, as long as the exemption code is permanently attached now. Chloe, it has been deeply distressing and humiliating having to fight for basic accessibility as a blind pensioner! Managing alone on a disability pension is already terrifying without S-Net penalising me!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have submitted a credit adjustment of three pounds fifty directly onto your current ledger balance.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will that reduce my next direct debit payment automatically?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, your next monthly collection will be discounted by three pounds fifty, reducing it to twenty-six pounds fifty instead of thirty pounds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is wonderful, thank you Chloe.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also set a high-contrast text flag on your customer file so any written notices or letters arrive in eighteen-point high-contrast typeface.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will make such a massive difference to my daily independence.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can also request audio CD format or braille statements in the future if your visual needs ever change, Fatima.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Large print is perfect for now, but it is comforting to know audio format is available.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we conclude our call, that account contact telephone number was 0113 496 0882, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 0113 496 0882 is my landline.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We have waived the three pound fifty fee, credited your ledger, and attached the permanent large-print accessibility exemption to your profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You have sorted out everything I needed. Thank you so much for your help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other aspect of your S-Net billing or services I can assist you with today, Fatima?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your next monthly paper statement will dispatch on the twelfth of next month in your large print format.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will look out for the postman bringing the large print envelope next month.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our customer care team remains available seven days a week for any future accessibility adjustments.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is very reassuring to know S-Net has dedicated accessibility support.
